# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (best overall).** Runner's World picks these as best overall. They list at $299 and were $199 at the time of writing. Their clip design is comfortable and the audio quality is excellent. RTINGS says they're slightly better for most people than the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2. They're more portable, put no pressure on your cheekbones or temples, and are slightly more stable. Downsides are the price and occasional glitches with Immersive Audio.
- Sources: [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [RTINGS comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)

**Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (best bone conduction).** WIRED rated it 8/10, calling it a great fit for running with big sound and USB-C charging. It has an IP55 rating, so it handles sweat and rinsing but not swimming. WIRED's review listed it at $180, with $125 deals at REI and Best Buy, though that review is from 2024, so check current pricing. RTINGS notes it has multi-device pairing and a tougher build than the Bose, and it suits people with many ear piercings.
- Sources: [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [RTINGS comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)

**Shokz OpenDots 2 (best for long runs and bad weather).** WIRED's top open-earbud pick costs $200. It has 10 hours of battery (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating, and the top of your ear stays free for sunglasses or a hat. Runner's World also names it best for long runs.
- Sources: [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/), [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Soundcore AeroFit 2 (best value).** It has IP55 water resistance, weighs 10 g per bud, and gets 10 hours per charge (42 with the case). SoundGuys calls it their best budget pick at $79.99 on Amazon. Dealectric lists it at $129.99, or $104 with code AFSC20, which they say they last tested on 2026-10-22. The prices differ a lot, so compare before buying.
- [Buy at Soundcore via Dealectric (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2)
- Sources: [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/), [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-open-ear-earbuds-for-running-2026-review-comparison-shokz-openrun-pro-2-sou)

**Other options:**
- **Nothing Ear (Open):** SoundGuys' best overall open pick and their best for running. It was $99 on Amazon, down from $149 ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)).
- **JLab Flex Open:** Runner's World's budget pick ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)).

## Quick guidance
- **Most people:** Bose Ultra Open.
- **Maximum awareness, or you dislike anything on the ear:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.
- **Rain, long runs, or glasses and hats:** Shokz OpenDots 2.
- **Tight budget:** AeroFit 2 or Nothing Ear (Open).

Open-ear designs leak some sound and have no noise cancelling, so people next to you may hear your audio. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.

I only have the Dealectric purchase link, so for the others I can't give direct retailer URLs. The review pages above link to Amazon, Best Buy, and the brands' own stores.
